newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU bans fish imports from India and Bangladesh.
newsitem.headline: EU bans fish imports from India and Bangladesh.

text.p: The European Commission, citing health and safety concerns, said on Monday it had banned fishery products from Bangladesh, India and Madagascar.

The decision to halt imports of products such as shrimp and squid from the three countries, last year valued at some 320 million European currency units ($338 million), was temporary and would be reviewed before November 30, the European Union executive said.

"The decisions result from visits by inspectors from the Commission's Food and Veterinary Office, who recently inspected fish processing plants in the three countries concerned," it said in a statement.
"The inspections showed serious deficiencies in the structure of establishments, the hygiene quality of raw material, and in processing operations."
The inspections also showed that the level of control by the national authorities was inadequate, an important factor in the decision to opt for total bans, the Commission said.
The bans have already taken effect, although fish products which are being shipped to the 15-nation EU may be admitted before August 15, subject to satisfactory sample testing.
"The latter date will be reconsidered by the Standing Veterinary Committee and the Commission next week, and may be extended," the Commission said.
Last year, Britain, Belgium, Italy, Spain, France, Portugal and the Netherlands were among EU countries importing fish products from at least one of the three countries concerned. ($=0.95 Ecu)
